title: Bonjour, mes amis!
oneGoal: Students will recognize and respond to basic French greetings through gestures and visual cues
decisionPoints: How comfortable are students with new sounds?
What level of gestures/TPR support is needed?
Should we extend listening time before expecting responses?
progression: Foundation lesson - establishes safety and comfort with French sounds and basic classroom routines
realWorldConnection: How people greet each other in French-speaking communities around the world

title: Je m'appelle...
oneGoal: Students will understand name introductions and begin to share their names using gestures and visual supports
decisionPoints: Are students ready to say their names or still observing?
How much repetition is needed for name patterns?
Should we use more visual name cards or gestures?
progression: Builds on Lesson 1 by adding personal identity while maintaining the greeting foundation
realWorldConnection: How introductions work in French families and communities

title: Les couleurs magiques
oneGoal: Students will recognize and respond to basic color words through visual objects and movement
decisionPoints: Which colors are students naturally drawn to?
Should we use more movement games or quiet observation?
Are students ready for color-matching activities?
progression: Builds on Lesson 2 by introducing first concrete vocabulary while reinforcing greetings and names
realWorldConnection: Describing the colorful world around us - flowers, toys, clothes

title: Mes premiers nombres
oneGoal: Students will recognize numbers 1-5 through finger counting, songs, and visual representations
decisionPoints: How are students responding to finger counting?
Should we focus on listening or include some speaking?
Are visual number cards helping comprehension?
progression: Builds on Lesson 3 by adding mathematical vocabulary while spiraling colors and greetings
realWorldConnection: Counting everyday things - toys, books, fingers, age

title: Ma famille française
oneGoal: Students will understand family words through photos, drawings, and inclusive family representations
decisionPoints: How do we honor diverse family structures?
Are students ready to share about their families?
Should we use more visual supports or storytelling?
progression: Builds on Lesson 4 by introducing personal/emotional vocabulary while reinforcing numbers and colors
realWorldConnection: How French-speaking families talk about themselves and show love

title: Les animaux amusants
oneGoal: Students will recognize animal names through sounds, movements, and visual supports
decisionPoints: Which animal movements engage students most?
Should we include animal sounds or focus on names?
Are students ready for simple animal classification?
progression: Builds on Lesson 5 by expanding vocabulary categories while practicing family words and numbers
realWorldConnection: Animals in our neighborhoods, farms, and French-speaking countries

title: Mes parties du corps
oneGoal: Students will identify basic body parts through songs, movements, and touching exercises
decisionPoints: How comfortable are students with body part songs?
Should we use mirrors or partner activities?
Are movement games helping or overwhelming?
progression: Builds on Lesson 6 by introducing body vocabulary while incorporating animal movements and family concepts
realWorldConnection: Taking care of our bodies and describing ourselves to others

title: Les objets de classe
oneGoal: Students will recognize classroom objects through touch, pointing, and simple commands
decisionPoints: Which classroom objects are most meaningful to students?
Should we use scavenger hunts or direct instruction?
Are students ready for simple following directions?
progression: Builds on Lesson 7 by connecting to immediate environment while practicing body parts and previous vocabulary
realWorldConnection: Using French to navigate and organize our learning space

title: J'aime et je n'aime pas
oneGoal: Students will express simple preferences through gestures, facial expressions, and visual supports
decisionPoints: How are students showing preferences non-verbally?
Should we focus on positive expressions first?
Are students ready for simple choice-making activities?
progression: Builds on Lesson 8 by introducing preference language while applying all previously learned vocabulary
realWorldConnection: Expressing what we like and don't like about food, activities, and things around us

title: Les actions quotidiennes
oneGoal: Students will understand basic action words through demonstration, mime, and physical response
decisionPoints: Which actions naturally engage student energy levels?
Should we use more demonstration or student participation?
Are movement breaks helping or disrupting flow?
progression: Builds on Lesson 9 by adding action vocabulary while practicing preferences and classroom objects
realWorldConnection: Describing what we do every day at home and school

title: Les saisons et météo
oneGoal: Students will recognize weather and season words through window observations, clothing, and sensory experiences
decisionPoints: How does current weather connect to lesson content?
Should we go outside or use window observations?
Are clothing props helping comprehension?
progression: Builds on Lesson 10 by connecting actions to environmental contexts while spiraling all previous vocabulary
realWorldConnection: Talking about weather and seasons affects our daily choices and activities

title: Mes émotions en français
oneGoal: Students will identify basic emotion words through facial expressions, body language, and scenarios
decisionPoints: How are students expressing emotions non-verbally?
Should we use mirrors, photos, or dramatic play?
Are students ready to connect emotions to experiences?
progression: Builds on Lesson 11 by adding emotional vocabulary while connecting to weather, actions, and preferences
realWorldConnection: Understanding and expressing how we feel in different situations

title: Notre routine française
oneGoal: Students will understand daily routine vocabulary through sequencing, clocks, and role-play activities
decisionPoints: How do student daily routines connect to lesson content?
Should we use picture schedules or physical demonstrations?
Are students ready for simple time concepts?
progression: Builds on Lesson 12 by organizing all previous vocabulary into daily life patterns and emotional contexts
realWorldConnection: How French-speaking children structure their days and talk about time

title: Ma petite présentation
oneGoal: Students will demonstrate understanding through simple presentation combining all learned vocabulary and concepts
decisionPoints: What format best supports each student's comfort level?
Should presentations be individual, pairs, or small groups?
How can we celebrate progress while acknowledging silent period?
progression: Builds on Lesson 13 by synthesizing all previous lessons into personalized demonstrations of French understanding
realWorldConnection: Sharing ourselves with others builds community and confidence in language learning

title: Jeux et chansons françaises
oneGoal: Students will practice all vocabulary through games, songs, and playful activities (extension/enrichment)
decisionPoints: Which games best reinforce learning without pressure?
Should we focus on group or individual activities?
Are students ready for more complex play patterns?
progression: Extension of Lesson 14 - focuses on joyful practice and application of all previous learning
realWorldConnection: Playing and having fun are universal ways children learn and connect

title: Histoires et images
oneGoal: Students will engage with simple French stories through pictures, gestures, and interactive storytelling (extension/enrichment)
decisionPoints: Which story elements capture student attention?
Should we use big books, digital stories, or props?
Are students ready for story prediction activities?
progression: Extension of Lesson 15 - deepens language exposure through narrative and visual literacy
realWorldConnection: Stories help us understand different perspectives and connect across cultures

title: Art et créativité française
oneGoal: Students will create visual art while using French vocabulary for colors, shapes, and creative expression (extension/enrichment)
decisionPoints: How do students best express creativity while using French?
Should we focus on process or product?
Are collaborative or individual projects more engaging?
progression: Extension of Lesson 16 - integrates artistic expression with language practice and cultural exploration
realWorldConnection: Art is a universal language that complements verbal communication

title: Cuisiner et goûter
oneGoal: Students will explore French food vocabulary through safe tasting, cooking activities, and cultural exploration (extension/enrichment)
decisionPoints: How do we accommodate dietary restrictions and preferences?
Should we prepare food or use pictures and props?
Are students ready for cultural food discussions?
progression: Extension of Lesson 17 - connects language to cultural experiences and sensory learning
realWorldConnection: Food brings families and communities together across all cultures

title: Musique et mouvement
oneGoal: Students will explore French through music, rhythm, and coordinated movement activities (extension/enrichment)
decisionPoints: How does music enhance or challenge student attention?
Should we use recorded music or create our own sounds?
Are students ready for partner or group choreography?
progression: Extension of Lesson 18 - integrates kinesthetic learning with rhythm and musical expression
realWorldConnection: Music and movement are joyful ways people celebrate and communicate in every culture

title: Notre célébration française
oneGoal: Students will celebrate their French learning journey through showcase activities, reflection, and community sharing (extension/enrichment)
decisionPoints: How do we honor each student's unique learning journey?
Should celebration be classroom-focused or include families?
What format best demonstrates growth while respecting silent period?
progression: Extension of Lesson 19 - culminates the entire unit with celebration, reflection, and community building
realWorldConnection: Celebrating learning achievements builds confidence and motivation for continued language exploration
